title: Working from Roofs
summary: In construction, falls from higher levels cause more deaths and injuries than any other cause, and many are falls from rooftops. Use fall protection any time the drop is 6 feet or more.
talking_points: Falls from higher levels result in more deaths and injuries than any other cause in construction. Many are falls from rooftops.
Fall protection is required for anyone working on roofs or other areas where the distance to the ground or another surface is 6 feet or more.
Roofing slide guards are not fall protection.
Always inspect your fall arrest equipment for damage.
If fall arrest equipment looks like it needs repair, remove it from service and have an expert examine it.
Ask your supervisor about adding permanent anchorages during roofing operations.
Permanent anchorages must support 5,000 pounds for each person attached to them by a lanyard or a lifeline.
Bill slipped on a garage roof about 10 feet up and nearly slid off. His harness and lifeline stopped the fall.
site_hazards_to_check: Roof edges where the drop to the ground or another surface is 6 feet or more
Slippery roof surfaces where a worker could slide toward the edge
Roofing slide guards being used as the only protection
Anchorages that are missing or not rated for 5,000 pounds per person
discussion_questions: What is the purpose of a lifeline?
Do you know anyone who has fallen off a rooftop? What happened?
What will we do at this worksite to prevent falls from rooftops?

flags: All points quote-accurate to the CPWR Toolbox Talk "Preventing Falls from Rooftops" (2017); the source itself cites OSHA 1926.501-1926.502, which are correct.
FIX: the source says "more than 6 feet"; the regulation (1926.501(b)(1), (b)(13)) triggers at 6 feet or more, so wording was corrected in summary, talking point, and hazard list.

Non-blocking: talk is narrow (fall protection only; no ladder access or skylight points), but has 6 substantive points plus the story. Consider "competent person" instead of "an expert" for gear inspection.
